requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the source generator and analyzer from crashing when a [MessagePackObject] type has a member whose type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. Two diagnostic paths in TypeCollector used to index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`; they now use `FirstOrDefault()`. Separately, every diagnostic TypeCollector reports now goes through a new filter that drops any diagnostic without a source location in the current compilation. The change adds three tests that compile a defining assembly to metadata and reference it, plus README and MsgPack004 doc text explaining that such types' member diagnostics belong to the defining project.
story.why: For metadata symbols `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty, so indexing `[0]` threw `IndexOutOfRangeException`. That crashed the analyzer (AD0001) and made the generator emit nothing (CS8785), which silently removed the resolver.
touches_beyond_requirement: A global diagnostic filter (`ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`) now wraps every diagnostic TypeCollector reports, not only the crashing paths. It also drops diagnostics with `Location.None` for types declared in source.
New README section and new MsgPack004 doc section describing user-visible diagnostic behaviour for types from referenced assemblies.
Test helper that builds its own compilation and generator driver outside the verifier.
story.confidence_overview: High that the two edited `[0]` sites can no longer throw. Medium that no other unguarded `[0]` remains: the issue names three sites and only two edits are visible. Medium-to-low on side effects of the global filter. Low that the tests prove the resolver is generated: that assertion is vacuous and the expected hint name is never used.

refusals.what: Test helper claims to verify that the expected resolver is generated but asserts only `NotNull` on a list that can never be null, and ignores `expectedResolverHintName`.
refusals.why: The test checks nothing for the key symptom (missing resolver) while its documentation says it does.

refusals.what: Global diagnostic suppression for any non-source location, plus documentation that declares this as intended analyzer behaviour.
refusals.why: This goes beyond the crash fix and changes which diagnostics users see, including possibly some for their own source types. The owner should decide whether that policy is wanted.

findings.description: Claim C1 disputed: TypeCollector.cs lines 985 and 1434 replace DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] with GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item), but neither named test exercises BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull: ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference (line 517) and ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference (line 559) both use [Key(0)], so intKey == null && stringKey == null at line 983 is never entered. Also, GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null not only when a property has no source declaration, but also for source-declared positional record properties whose syntax node is ParameterSyntax rather than PropertyDeclarationSyntax.

Claim C6 disputed: The claim contradicts itself: its first sentence states that the tests verify a resolver is actually generated in the consuming assembly, which is false and leaves the cited requirement untested. VerifyCS.Test sets TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck (line 641), expectedResolverHintName (line 633) is never used, line 656 only checks DiagnosticSeverity.Error (CS8785 is a warning and GeneratorRunResult.Exception is unchecked), and Assert.NotNull(hintNames) (lines 657-658) tests a List<string> from .ToList() that is never null even when zero files are generated.

`Assert.NotNull(hintNames)` can never fail because `ToList()` never returns null. The `expectedResolverHintName` parameter is never asserted on. The doc comment at lines 629-631 claims resolver generation is verified, so the test overstates its coverage of the 'no resolver' symptom.

Only diagnostics of Error severity are rejected. CS8785 (generator failure) is a warning, so this second check would not catch the original defect. Detection relies entirely on the VerifyCS run at line 648.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source. That includes diagnostics for types declared in the current compilation that are created with a null or `Location.None` location (for example when a FirstOrDefault-based helper returns null). Such diagnostics were previously reported and are now silently suppressed, which is a broad behaviour change beyond the crash fix.

The issue names three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (735, 1009, 1101 in 3.1.8), but only two are edited. Nothing in the diff shows a site near line 735 being addressed, so another crash path may remain for other metadata-type shapes.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops any diagnostic where diagnostic.Location.IsInSource is false, which silently swallows diagnostics with Location.None even for symbols declared in the current compilation. For example, GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (line 1434) uses 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax', returning null for source-declared positional record or record struct properties (whose syntax is ParameterSyntax), so BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull on [property: Key((string)null)] in the current compilation gets Location.None and is dropped; similarly, any in-compilation diagnostic using GetParameterListLocation (line 1454) when method is null or implicit gets Location.None and is silently suppressed.

In the other branch of the ternary right above the MemberNeedsKey fix, derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken).GetLocation() is called when derivedKeyAttribute is not null and suppressSourceGeneration is not true. For a closed generic value type from metadata, an attribute derived from KeyAttribute has no syntax in source, so dereferencing GetSyntax(...).GetLocation() will throw NullReferenceException and crash both the generator (CS8785) and analyzer (AD0001).
